input_contract.retrieval_statement: This model reads the values saved in the committed morning panel. Each key is resolved through the declared source catalogue (provider, series, transform and publication lag) and every value carries either a contemporaneous capture with a receipt taken at or before the cutoff, or an explicit reconstruction digest. The n8n Cloud child replays the saved values; it does not fetch history, so a replay alone never establishes historical availability.
input_contract.source_clock_policy: contemporaneous only when a capture at or before the cutoff matches the replayed value and carries a receipt id; otherwise reconstructed_panel with no receipt
input_contract.fill_policy: the controller never fills a missing value and never estimates one

models.cloud_note: The production-control adapter reads local files and warehouse helpers, so it is deliberately not bundled into the n8n Cloud runtime.

keys.rule: VIX above 25 is safe-haven USD demand; below 16 is risk-on pressure
a 5-day VIX rise of more than one index point bids USD; a fall of the same size releases it
front-end yields up more than 5bp support USD; down more than 5bp oppose it
real yields up more than 5bp support USD; down more than 5bp oppose it
the dollar's own 5-day move continues: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD strength and a fall as weakness; FRED DTWEXBGS stands in for ICE DXY and is labelled as such everywhere
gold up more than 0.5% is a hedge bid against USD; down more than 0.5% is the reverse
equities up more than 0.5% is risk-on and reads against USD; down more than 0.5% reads for it
EUR/USD is USD inverted: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD weakness and a fall as USD strength; it stands in for the German 2-year leg the current model cannot reconstruct, and says so
USD/JPY is USD direct: a rise above 0.15% is read as USD strength and a fall as weakness

agreement.note: Agreement between two books is a reproduction observation, not an accuracy or an edge claim.

labels.research_only: Research only. Gross directional replay with no costs, no slippage and no execution.
labels.fixture_policy: A fixture is a registered test double. It is labelled a fixture, excluded from research deltas, and never described as a book.
labels.validation: Structural validity only: internal consistency and the declared 05:00 London cutoff. Receipted validity is reported separately and is zero on this panel.

consistency.statement: Each stored call reproduces in the local controller, and its hit/miss/flat arithmetic recomputes from the committed outcomes.

historical_availability.statement: The children replayed the committed panel. No retrieval receipt or source archive is recorded, so nothing here shows the values were available at the cutoff.

model_logic.statement: Parity compares the frozen rules with themselves. No independent adjudication exists, so correct logic is not demonstrated.

coverage.statement: The panel is a research artefact; it is not proven to equal what a live 05:00 run would have offered on each date.

cutoff_contract.note: 05:00 London is midnight in New York in both GMT and BST, so the session starts on the New York calendar day boundary and each eligible session is exactly 24 hours long

historical_validity.note: Structural validity is internal consistency plus the declared 05:00 London cutoff. Receipted validity additionally requires a full timestamp before the cutoff for every consumed input. The committed panel has no stamped print after the cutoff, so a genuine late-print rejection is not demonstrated by history; it remains untested rather than inferred.

parity.note: Reproduction of the stored calls only. These figures are not accuracy and not an edge claim.

cloud_bundle.note: The generated Cloud bundle reproduced the Node controller for both challengers over all 725 mornings.

performance.note: Gross directional replay, structural validation only, no costs, no slippage, no live execution and no multiple-testing or holdout claim. Test 1 is a broker proxy; tests 3 and 4 are blocked. Report this separately from reproduction and from the validation gate.

limitations: n8n Cloud does not provide Execute Command, so the original host-command workflows cannot run there; the Cloud workflows bundle the controller instead.
The production-control adapter is not in the Cloud runtime; only the two frozen challengers are.
No committed morning has a stamped print after the 05:00 cutoff, so late-print rejection is untested on history.
The receipted gate refuses every one of the 725 committed mornings because most macro prints carry a date only.
The evidence covers four controlled dates, not a full n8n batch. The local controller remains the 725-morning batch path.
H1 is unscored and is not one of the two n8n children.
next_actions: Acquire a 05:00 receipt archive with full timestamps for the inputs the challengers consume, then rerun the receipted gate.
Record a late-print fixture separately and label it synthetic; do not add it to historical validity.
If the production-control adapter must run in n8n Cloud, package its replay dependencies explicitly instead of assuming filesystem access.
